title: General relativity, early galaxy formation and the JWST observations
efc_relevance: A purely relativistic, GR-only mechanism (peculiar-velocity flux in the energy-momentum tensor) that raises the linear growth rate from delta proportional to t^(2/3) to delta proportional to t, argued to accommodate massive early galaxies without new physics or fine-tuning. It is a competing THEORY for the same observable EFC addresses with a regime-gated early boost (atlas addressing EFC -> early_structure_JWST, S_flow_boost_at_high_z). The two are separable in principle: this mechanism is not regime-gated and would raise growth broadly, while EFC's is damped (mu<1) and late.
ledger_action: Recorded in the Atlas external-evidence register (FRAG-TSAGAS-PECULIAR-FLUX) as an alternative explanation, linked to early_structure_JWST and sigma8_growth. No Validation Ledger row: the essay contains no data comparison, so it cannot carry an empirical status.
